title: Compactifications and refinements
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]; when $S$ is a finite-field scheme, impose the geometric
hypotheses [def-weil-geometric-hypotheses]. Let $X$ and $Y$ be finite-type
[def-weil-finite-type-morphism] $S$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-over-base], and let $f:X\to Y$ be a
separated [def-weil-proper-morphism] finite-type $S$-morphism. A *compactification* $c=(j,\bar f)$ of
$f$ is a factorization

$$
 X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{\bar f}Y
$$

with $j$ an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], $\bar f$ a proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] $S$-morphism
($\overline X$ being an $S$-scheme through $\bar f$ and $Y\to S$), and $\bar f\circ
j=f$. A *refinement* $u:c_1\to c_2$ is a proper $Y$-morphism ($\overline X_i$ being a $Y$-scheme through $\bar f_i$)

$$
 u:\overline X_1\longrightarrow\overline X_2
$$

such that $u\circ j_1=j_2$. Compactifications and refinements form a category [def-nagata-category]
$\operatorname{Comp}(f)$, with the identity morphisms of the schemes $\overline X$ as identities and the
composition of morphisms of schemes as composition [lem-nagata-refinements-form-category].
